# Getting MICS6 data {#c01-getting-data}

This guide covers Round 6 of UNICEF's Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS6), the round that introduced the Foundational Learning Skills (FLS) module.

There are two ways to obtain the data:

1. UNICEF MICS — the original country files; or
2. IPUMS MICS — a customised, harmonised multi-country extract.

Which you use depends on the research question. Two constraints matter in practice: building an IPUMS extract currently requires a Stata licence, and a single-country analysis gains little from IPUMS harmonisation.

| | UNICEF MICS | IPUMS MICS |
|---|---|---|
| What you receive | Original country survey files | A customised extract with harmonised variables across selected surveys |
| Best for | Country-specific variables; the FLS assessment; reproducing or extending MICS indicators | Multi-country analysis of demographic, household, schooling and other background variables |
| Preparation required | More: files must be organised, merged and harmonised for multi-country work | Less: IPUMS supplies harmonisation syntax and combines the selected samples |
| Software required | Any: the `.sav` files open in R or Stata | Stata to build the extract. The resulting `.dta` can then be analysed in R or Stata |
| Single-country analysis | Recommended | Adds little: the benefit of IPUMS is cross-survey harmonisation |
| Foundational numeracy | Recommended | Can be used |
| Foundational reading | Recommended | Do not use the IPUMS reading variables in MICS6 surveys with more than one reading passage. IPUMS retains only one passage, so children assessed on other passages are missing. See [Adding the correct reading data to an IPUMS extract](#c04-ipums-reading). |

::: {.warningbox-header}
**AFLEARN recommendation**
:::

::: {.warningbox}
If the analysis uses foundational reading, do not use the IPUMS reading variables for countries that administered more than one passage. IPUMS retains only one passage and can exclude a large share of children who completed the assessment. AFLEARN provides a research-ready reading file built from the complete UNICEF source data, which you can merge onto an IPUMS extract.
:::

This chapter covers both downloads. [Getting data from UNICEF MICS](#c01-unicef) shows how to obtain the country files. [Organising the UNICEF download](#c01-organise) unpacks them and runs the AFLEARN preparation scripts. [Getting data from IPUMS MICS](#c01-ipums) shows how to build an extract.

UNICEF releases MICS microdata in their original survey-file structure. [IPUMS MICS](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/) is a collaboration that standardises variable names, coding and documentation across surveys. See the [IPUMS MICS Getting Started guide](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/user_guide.shtml). The two routes complement each other: IPUMS for harmonised background variables, UNICEF source files for complete foundational reading.
